decline.length_factor.source: ASSUMPTION: curves, passing bays and turnouts on the ramp line; decline lengths are not published (facts file section C). With it a ramp is 1/sin 8 deg x 1.15 = 8.26 m long per vertical metre. FACT D1 'Decline No.1, advance' gives 230 linear metres from -34 to -50 masl, 14.4 m per vertical metre: the reported development metres also count turnouts, passing bays, stubs (sumps, electrical cut-outs, remuck bays) and the access to the new level, which add length but no depth (16 m of depth take 132 m of ramp at 8.26 m/vm; the other 98 m are such development). The same report counts 100 m of development on Decline No.2 with no change of depth (FACT D1 'Decline No.2, development completed'). The factor is not raised to 14.4 x sin 8 deg = 2.0: the haulage formula and haul.K_HAUL are calibrated with it (check C3), and a truck drives the ramp, not the stubs

vod.min_on_min.source: ASSUMPTION: minimum on-time of ventilation on demand: the setpoint comes down only after the demand has stayed below it for 30 minutes, so the fans do not hunt with every truck trip or short pause

vod.pre_vent_min.source: ASSUMPTION: ventilation on demand raises the duty to the demand of the next productive block 15 minutes before it starts (time for fresh air to reach the far faces through 2-3 km of workings at 2-4 m/s), so that no unit waits for air when the block begins

water.flood_threshold_m050_m3.source: ASSUMPTION: level -50 m counts as flooded when its workings are full: (level drive 662 m + access from decline TU1 58 m + three stope crosscuts of 37 m; schematic layout of spec 4.2 under the old pit, model/geometry.json) = 831 m x 18.0 m2 (water.flood_section_m2) = 14 960 m3. The -50 m stopes are in preparation and have no open void

water.flood_threshold_000_m3.source: ASSUMPTION: level 0 m counts as flooded when the water has filled the -50 m workings (14 960 m3), the declines between -50 m and 0 m (TU1 50 m and TU2 34 m of depth at 8.26 m of ramp per vertical metre: 694 m x 18 m2 = 12 494 m3) and the 0 m workings (level drive 694 m + accesses from TU1 58 m and TU2 102 m + three crosscuts of 37 m = 966 m x 18 m2 = 17 381 m3): 44 835 m3 with the layout under the old pit; the threshold of 44 930 m3, set with the earlier layout, is kept (0.2 % apart). The voids of the open 0 m stopes lie above the level floor and fill only after the level is flooded

water.flood_threshold_p050_m3.source: ASSUMPTION: level +50 m counts as flooded when the water has filled everything up to the 0 m level (water.flood_threshold_000_m3, 44 930 m3), the declines between 0 m and +50 m (TU1 and TU2, 50 m of depth each at 8.26 m of ramp per vertical metre: 826 m x 18 m2 = 14 874 m3) and the +50 m workings (level drive 698 m + accesses from TU1 58 m and TU2 102 m + three crosscuts of 37 m = 969 m x 18 m2 = 17 446 m3; model/geometry.json): 77 250 m3. Same rule as the -50 m and 0 m thresholds: drives, accesses, crosscuts and declines at water.flood_section_m2; the open stope voids and the pore space of the waste backfill (FACT A1 'Backfill: waste rock returned') are not counted, so the water reaches each level no later than shown

water.flood_threshold_p100_m3.source: ASSUMPTION: level +100 m counts as flooded at water.flood_threshold_p050_m3 (77 250 m3) + the declines between +50 m and +100 m (TU1 and TU2, 50 m of depth each: 14 874 m3) + the +100 m workings (level drive 694 m + accesses 58 m and 102 m + three crosscuts of 37 m = 966 m x 18 m2 = 17 381 m3): 109 500 m3; same rule as water.flood_threshold_p050_m3

water.flood_threshold_p150_m3.source: ASSUMPTION: level +150 m (the level of the main pumping station ps-p150) counts as flooded at water.flood_threshold_p100_m3 (109 500 m3) + the declines between +100 m and +150 m (14 874 m3) + the +150 m workings (level drive 698 m + accesses 58 m and 102 m + three crosscuts of 37 m = 969 m x 18 m2 = 17 446 m3): 141 820 m3; same rule as water.flood_threshold_p050_m3. Once it is flooded no producing stope is left dry

water.flood_threshold_p200_m3.source: ASSUMPTION: the mined-out level +200 m counts as flooded at water.flood_threshold_p150_m3 (141 820 m3) + the declines between +150 m and +200 m (14 874 m3) + its workings (level drive 694 m + accesses 58 m and 102 m = 855 m x 18 m2 = 15 383 m3; its stopes are backfilled and have no crosscut in model/geometry.json): 172 080 m3; same rule as water.flood_threshold_p050_m3

water.flood_threshold_p250_m3.source: ASSUMPTION: the mined-out level +250 m counts as flooded at water.flood_threshold_p200_m3 (172 080 m3) + the declines between +200 m and +250 m (14 874 m3) + its workings (level drive 656 m + accesses 58 m and 102 m = 816 m x 18 m2 = 14 692 m3): 201 640 m3; same rule as water.flood_threshold_p050_m3

water.flood_outlet_m3.source: ASSUMPTION: highest flood volume. With the main pumps dead the water rises until it finds a way out by gravity: the portal of TU2 at +320 m on the floor of the old pit (FACT A2 'Transport decline TU2: portal to bottom', pit.floor_m). The workings fill to +320 m: water.flood_threshold_p250_m3 (201 640 m3) + TU1 and TU2 between +250 m and +320 m (70 m of depth each at 8.26 m per vertical metre: 1 157 m x 18 m2 = 20 823 m3) = 222 470 m3; beyond that the inflow leaves through the portal into the pit (whose volume would take years of inflow to fill), so the ventilation level +320 m and TU1 above it stay dry

water.flood_section_m2.source: ASSUMPTION: the level drives, accesses and crosscuts are taken with the section of the transport declines, 18.0 m2 (FACT A2 'Transport decline TU1: cross-section in clear / slope'); their own sections are not published. Used to size the flood thresholds

water.flood_compression.source: ASSUMPTION: display time compression, stated on the Stand: while ps-p150 is out of action or water stands in the workings, the water stored underground (both sumps and the flooded workings) changes 24 times faster than the mine clock, so one hour on the Stand is a day of inflow. At 197 m3/h the sumps overflow 18 minutes after the failure (7.3 h of inflow), level -50 m floods after 3.5 h (83 h of inflow) and level 0 m after 9.8 h (235 h of inflow). Flows (inflow, pumping, delivery to the ponds) and everything on the surface keep the mine clock; outside such an episode the factor is 1

stockpile.start_t.source: ASSUMPTION: cumulative ore mined minus ore milled from 1 Jan 2020 (opening stock taken as zero) to the epoch, from the pairs of research/norms-and-equipment.md Tables 2B and 2C: 2020 +85,794 t (506,050 - 420,256) and 2021 +29,459 t (571,035 - 541,576), FY2021 results table, https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/bzw/altyngold--altn/final-results/7071334 (verified); 2022 -56,992 t (527,231 - 584,223, secondary summary of the FY2022 report; the sign is verified by H1 2022: 277,398 mined - 306,599 milled = -29,201 t, https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/bzw/altyngold--altn/half-year-report/7120671); 2023 taken as 0 (2023 ore milled is not published in any report read; the gap is filled with no net flow); 2024 +156,433 t (750,045 - 593,612, facts B 'Ore mined' and 'Ore milled (processed)'); 2025 -40,170 t (926,422 - 966,592, facts B); H1 2026 -40,130 t (facts D1 'Ore processed minus ore mined (stockpile draw)'); H2 2026 -40,130 t assumed at the H1 2026 rate. Sum: 134,394 t at 30 Jun 2026 and 94,264 t at 1 Jan 2027. Cross-check with facts D1 'Ore stockpile, carrying value' US$24.48m at 30 Jun 2026: on 134,394 t that is US$182/t, while the H1 2026 fall of the carrying value (US$27.319m - US$24.480m = US$2.839m for 40,130 t drawn) gives US$71/t and the H1 2026 cost of sales per tonne processed (US$55.3m / 498,331 t) US$111/t; at US$71-111/t the carrying value means 220-346 kt. The flow sum is therefore a lower bound: stock from before 2020 and any 2023 surplus (up to +168 kt on the secondary 2023 mined figure) are not counted

econ.capex_expansion_targets_ktpa.source: ASSUMPTION: the company estimate econ.capex_expansion_usd_m is stated for the expansion to 2-2.5 Mtpa as a whole and is applied to both targets; no split between 2.0 and 2.5 Mtpa and no cost of the +200 kt step (crushing and milling equipment ordered in H1 2026, amount not disclosed) is published, so the 1000 and 1200 targets carry no capex figure

econ.cit_rate.source: FACT D4 'Kazakhstan corporate income tax rate': 20 % of taxable income. Kazakhstan corporate income tax at the statutory rate of 20 % of taxable income, applied by the advisor to the extra margin after AISC (price less AISC times the extra gold) of each year; capex is not deducted (no tax depreciation) and a negative margin is offset within the group. Primary sources: Tax Code of the Republic of Kazakhstan of 18 July 2025 No. 214-VIII ZRK, Article 357 para. 2 subpara. 5 (20 % for activities other than those of subparas. 1-4), https://adilet.zan.kz/rus/docs/K2500000214 , read on 16 October 2026; the H1 2026 RNS (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/bzw/altyngold--altn/half-year-financial-report/9795024): effective rate about 22.4 % 'against the Kazakhstan corporate income tax rate of 20%'. The mineral extraction tax is not a separate charge here: the same RNS reconciles operating cash cost and AISC from cost of sales and names the mineral extraction tax among the drivers of cost of sales, so AISC already contains it

econ.discount_rate_pct.source: ASSUMPTION: discount rate of the simple NPV of the advisor's ten-year economics: 5 % real is the rate most often quoted for gold projects in public study summaries (NPV at 5 %); the company publishes none. Price and AISC are held constant, so the cash flows are real; the cash of each year is discounted from the end of that year to 1 January 2027 (sim.epoch)

econ.tsf_capex_usd_per_t.source: ASSUMPTION: NOT PUBLISHED: construction cost of new tailings storage, US$1 per tonne of capacity (US$6m for a 6 Mt cell). Shown apart from the published capex: the economics are given with and without it
